words.gloss: powder of śirīṣa, udumbara and śamī

hindi: शिरीष, उदुम्बर और शमी का चूर्ण घी के साथ मिलाकर तैयार किया हुआ आधे मास का क्षुद्-योग।
english: Powder of śirīṣa, udumbara and śamī, having been combined with ghee: the half-month hunger preparation.
notes: śirīṣa, udumbara, śamī are tree names; not identified. kṣud-yoga rendered literally as 'hunger preparation' (yoga = preparation, as in the rest of this chapter); the e-text gives no verb. ardha-māsika = lasting/for half a month. The edition joins saṃhṛtya-ardha with '-' (unsandhied join).

words.gloss: cooked with kaśeruka, utpala, tuber, sugarcane, root, lotus-fibre, dūrvā, milk, ghee and maṇḍa

hindi: कशेरुक, उत्पल, कन्द, ईख, मूल, बिस, दूर्वा, दूध, घी और मण्ड के साथ पकाया हुआ मासिक योग।
english: Cooked with kaśeruka, utpala, tuber, sugarcane, root, lotus-fibre, dūrvā, milk, ghee and maṇḍa: the monthly [preparation].
notes: 'kandekṣu' is split kanda + ikṣu (tuber, sugarcane); the alternative is a single plant name. maṇḍa is left as maṇḍa (scum/cream or rice-water are possible senses). The final noun (yoga) is supplied in brackets in English; Hindi says मासिक योग following unit 1. The list may also be read as '(in) the maṇḍa of milk and ghee'.

words.gloss: powder of roots of māṣa, yava, kulattha and darbha
paste of roots of sāla and pṛśniparṇī

hindi: उड़द, जौ, कुलत्थ और दर्भ की जड़ों का चूर्ण दूध और घी के साथ, या बेल, दूध और घी समान भाग में पकाया हुआ, या साल और पृश्निपर्णी की जड़ों की कल्क को दूध के साथ पीकर, या उससे पकाया हुआ दूध शहद और घी के साथ खाकर, वह एक मास तक उपवास करता है।
english: Powder of the roots of māṣa, yava, kulattha and darbha with milk and ghee; or creeper, milk and ghee cooked in equal [parts]; or having drunk with milk a paste of the roots of sāla and pṛśniparṇī, or milk cooked with that, having eaten [it] with honey and ghee, he fasts for a month.
notes: The text gives no subject; 'he' is supplied from upavasati. mūla in the first compound could also be read as 'roots' of darbha only; rendered as roots of all four. 'sama-siddham' = cooked in equal [parts] is the literal sense; the e-text splits pṛśni.parṇī as printed. Scope of 'aśitvā' (the powder, or the cooked milk) is not stated.

words.gloss: in the urine of a white goat
kept a month or half a month

hindi: सफेद बकरे के मूत्र में सात रात रखे गए सिद्धार्थकों के साथ पकाया हुआ तेल, जो कड़वी लौकी में एक मास या आधे मास रखा गया हो, चौपायों और दोपायों को कुरूप करना है।
english: Oil cooked with siddhārthaka [seeds] that have stayed seven nights in the urine of a white goat, and kept a month or half a month in a bitter gourd, is the making misshapen of quadrupeds and bipeds.
notes: siddhārthaka kept as a name, not identified. 'māsa-ardha-māsa' = a month or a half-month. Both 'quadrupeds and bipeds' as literal; sense of 'making misshapen' is virūpa-karaṇa.

words.gloss: of one whose food is buttermilk and barley

hindi: जो सफेद गधा छाछ और जौ खाता हो, उसकी सात रातों के बाद की लीद के जौ के साथ पकाया हुआ गौर सरसों का तेल कुरूप करना है।
english: After seven nights, the pale mustard oil cooked with the dung-barley of a white donkey whose food is buttermilk and barley is the making misshapen.
notes: leṇḍa = dung; 'leṇḍa-yava' rendered literally as 'dung-barley' (barley grains in the dung is a likely sense, not stated). Hindi uses लीद for leṇḍa. The construction 'sapta-rātrād ūrdhvam' qualifies the feeding: seven nights after it begins; the alternative reading is seven nights after the dung is collected.

words.gloss: cooked with urine, dung and juice
with an admixture of powder of arka floss and pataṅga

hindi: इन दोनों में से किसी एक के मूत्र, लीद और रस के साथ पकाया हुआ सिद्धार्थक का तेल, जिसमें अर्क की रुई और पतंग का चूर्ण मिलाया गया हो, सफेद करना है।
english: Siddhārthaka oil cooked with the urine, dung and juice of either of these two, with an admixture of powder of arka floss and pataṅga, is the whitening.

text_flags.why: typo: leṇda has dental d (Devanagari द); leṇḍa with retroflex ḍ is used elsewhere in this chunk (units 5, 7)

notes: 'etayor anyatarasya' = of either of these two (the goat and donkey of units 4-5); the animal is not named here. rasa rendered 'juice' literally (Glossary: rasa = poison only in poisoning contexts). arka-tūla = floss of arka (not identified); pataṅga left as name (insect or plant). pratīvāpa = admixture.

words.gloss: preparation of the dung of a white cock and ajagara

hindi: सफेद मुर्गे और अजगर की लीद का योग सफेद करना है।
english: A preparation of the dung of a white cock and of an ajagara is the whitening.
notes: 'śveta' may qualify only kukkuṭa (assumed), or both. ajagara taken literally as the large snake (python); the alternative is a plant name.

words.gloss: in the urine of a white goat

hindi: सफेद बकरे के मूत्र में सात रात रखे गए सफेद सरसों, छाछ, अर्क का दूध, नमक और अनाज, पक्ष भर रखा हुआ यह योग सफेद करना है।
english: White mustard seeds [kept] seven nights in the urine of a white goat, buttermilk, arka milk, salt and grain: the preparation kept for a fortnight is the whitening.

text_flags.why: possible: the editors' doubt mark; 'astakra(?).marka' read as 'uṣitās takra' + 'arka' (stray m); not certain

notes: Damaged token (the editors mark '(?)'). Reading uṣitāḥ + takra + arka-kṣīra + lavaṇa is only a possible repair; the English brackets show a supplied 'kept'. Alternative: 'astakra' is a different word. 'arka milk' = milky sap or milk of arka (plant not identified).

words.gloss: kept until half a month has passed

hindi: कड़वी लौकी में, जो झुर्रीदार हो गई हो, आधा मास बीतने तक रखा हुआ पिसा हुआ गौर सरसों रोमों को सफेद करना है।
english: Ground pale mustard, kept in a bitter gourd that has gone to wrinkles until half a month has passed, is the whitening of hairs.

text_flags.why: possible: the anusvāra after gata looks like a typo for a compound join (gata-ardha)
possible: valī (fold, wrinkle) is rendered literally; vallī (creeper) is the alternative

notes: 'valī-gate' is obscure: rendered literally as 'gone to wrinkles' (i.e. wrinkled); alternative 'gone to creepers/vine'. 'gata-ardha-māsa-sthita' read as 'kept [until] half a month has gone'; alternative 'kept for a half-month'.

hindi: जो कीट अलोजुन कहलाता है और सफेद गृह-गोलिका, इस पिसे हुए से लेप किए गए केश शंख के समान श्वेत हो जाएँ।
english: The insect that is called alojuna, and the white house-golikā: hairs anointed with this, [once] ground, would be conch-white.

text_flags.why: typo: piṣtena has dental t (पिष्तेन); piṣṭena (retroflex ṭ) is expected

notes: 'alojuneti' = alojuna + iti; alojuna is a name, not identified. 'gṛha-golikā' kept literally (house-golikā); a house-lizard is a possible sense but is not stated. The ground mass is of the insect and the golikā together (not stated). 'abhyaktāḥ' with '-' is an unsandhied join in the e-text.

words.gloss: with a paste of tinduka and ariṣṭa
of one whose limbs are rubbed

hindi: जिसके अंग गोबर से या तिन्दुक और अरिष्ट की कल्क से मले गए हों और भल्लातक के रस से लेप किए गए हों, उसके लिए मासिक कुष्ठ-योग।
english: For one whose limbs are rubbed with cow-dung or with a paste of tinduka and ariṣṭa, and smeared with bhallātaka juice: the monthly kuṣṭha preparation.
notes: tinduka, ariṣṭa, bhallātaka are plant names; not identified. rasa = juice. kuṣṭha kept as kuṣṭha. 'For one whose ...' follows the genitives mardita-aṅgasya / anuliptasya; the construction is elliptical.

words.gloss: in the mouth of a black snake
in the mouth of a house-golikā

hindi: काले सर्प के मुख में या गृह-गोलिका के मुख में सात रात रखी गई गुञ्जाएँ कुष्ठ-योग हैं।
english: Guñjā [seeds] that have stayed seven nights in the mouth of a black snake or in the mouth of a house-golikā: a kuṣṭha preparation.

text_flags.why: possible: gujjā may be a genuine Prakrit-like form; guñjā is the standard spelling

notes: guñjā seeds kept as name, not identified; 'seeds' is the usual sense but is a supplied word and is not stated in the text — rendered 'guñjā [seeds]'.

words.gloss: anointing with parrot bile and egg-juice

hindi: तोते के पित्त और अण्डे के रस का लेप कुष्ठ-योग है।
english: Anointing with the bile and egg-juice of a parrot: a kuṣṭha preparation.
notes: śuka taken as parrot (could be a plant name); pitta = bile (literal, not the humour). aṇḍa-rasa = egg-juice; whether 'parrot' governs the egg as well as the bile is not stated; alternative: 'bile, egg [and] juice'.

hindi: कुष्ठ का प्रतीकार प्रियाल की कल्क का काढ़ा है।
english: A decoction of priyāla paste is the remedy of kuṣṭha.

text_flags.why: possible: the editors' compound dot after the genitive kuṣṭhasya; it is probably a separate word

notes: priyāla is a plant name, not identified. 'kalka-kaṣāya' = decoction of paste (alternative: paste and decoction). pratīkāra = remedy.

words.gloss: combined with kukkuṭa, kośa, atakī and śatāvarī root

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. caus. ā-√hṛ

hindi: मुर्गा, कोश, अतकी और शतावरी की जड़ से युक्त आहार लेने वाला मनुष्य एक मास में गौर हो जाता है।
english: One who takes food combined with kukkuṭa, kośa, atakī and the root of śatāvarī becomes fair in a month.

text_flags.why: possible: the editors' doubt mark at atakī; 'kośa.atakī' may be one name, kośātakī

notes: Damaged word (doubt mark on atakī). Rendered literally as separate items; alternative: kukkuṭa and kośātakī (a plant name). 'kukkuṭa' could be the cock or a plant. The English object 'food' is supplied by āhārayamāṇaḥ. 'Man' in Hindi is supplied as the subject.

words.gloss: bathed in a decoction of vaṭa
smeared with a paste of sahacara

hindi: वट के काढ़े से स्नान किया हुआ और सहचर की कल्क से लिप्त मनुष्य काला हो जाता है।
english: One bathed in a decoction of vaṭa and smeared with a paste of sahacara becomes dark.
notes: vaṭa and sahacara are plant names, not identified; sahacara literally 'companion'. kṛṣṇa = dark/black.
